GALWAY WEST BYE-ELECTION – REGISTER OF ELECTORS 
 
The Galway West by-election is scheduled for 22 May 2026, following the signing of the 
Polling Day Order by the Minister on writ 
day, 23 April 2026.   The election deadlines 
for the receipt of applications to register, 
update details, or apply for inclusion on the 
postal or special voters lists were Saturday, 
25 April 2026 for postal and special voters, 
and Tuesday, 5 May 2026 for inclusion on 
the Register of Electors. 
 
In advance of the Galway West bye-election, the Register of Electors team undertook 
significant work to ensure that an accurate and up-to-date register is available, while also 
meeting all tight statutory and operational timelines along with working closely with the 
Galway Returning Officer and her team.    
Throughout the preparation period, the team’s primary focus was on the timely processing 
of all applications received via CheckTheRegister, ensuring compliance with statutory 
deadlines and meeting timelines with the printers to facilitate the production of Polling 
Cards.    
A strong social media campaign was undertaken to raise public awareness of key electoral 
timelines and to encourage eligible electors to register, to ensure they have their voice for 
the upcoming Galway West Bye-Election. 
In total, 52,884 electors are registered for the Galway West constituency within County 
Galway. During the preparation period, the Register of Electors team received 673 new 
applications, 91 of which were from electors reaching voting age. In addition, 107 electors 
registered for a postal vote, and there are 212 special voters on the register.

THE NATIONAL FAMINE COMMEMORATION AT THE IRISH WORKHOUSE CENTRE, 
PORTUMNA 
The 19th National Famine Commemoration took place on Sunday, 17 May in the Irish 
Workhouse Centre in Portumna, County Galway in remembrance of all those who suffered, 
died or was forced to emigrate due to An Gorta Mór.  This was the first time the National 
Famine Commemoration has been held in County Galway since it was established in 2008.

11 
 
 
The Minister for Culture, Communications and Sport and the Chair of the National Famine 
Commemoration Committee, Patrick O’Donovan TD was in attendance.  
Taoiseach Micheál Martin TD officiated at the event and delivered the keynote address. The 
Most Reverend Luis Mariano Montemayor, Apostolic Nuncio and the Dean of the Diplomatic 
Corps and the Cathaoirleach took part in proceedings introducing the Cultural Programme.  
The event included military honours, cultural and community elements before culminating 
in a solemn wreath-laying ceremony by the Taoiseach, Minister for Culture, 
Communications and Sport and the Dean of the Diplomatic Corp.  
The event was broadcast live on the RTÉ News channel but will be available for replay on the 
RTÉ Player and on irishfamine.ie at a later date. 
Galway County Council hosted a welcome reception for the Diplomatic Corp prior to the 
commemoration and a reception for the 500 in attendance following the ceremony. 
Opened in 1852 and regarded as one of the most complete surviving complexes of its kind, 
the Irish Workhouse Centre, Portumna has become a hub for lectures, exhibitions and cultural 
events.   The Workhouse and recently restored and re-opened Courthouse hosted a wide 
range of community heritage events as part of the wider commemoration programme.  
 
Cathaoirleach of Galway County Council, Councillor David Collins commented: 
“The story of An Gorta Mór is deeply interwoven with the history and identity of the county 
of Galway, shaping communities across the county and its wider diaspora, including places 
such as Portumna, where loss, survival and emigration from that period can still be felt 
today. This event honours the memory of those who suffered or emigrated, acknowledges 
the strength and resilience of communities across this county, and encourages us to 
recognise the importance of compassion, dignity and solidarity in society Irish today. 
“It is a privilege for Galway County Council and the people of Portumna to host this 
significant national commemoration.”

MEETING WITH OIREACHTAS MEMBERS – 30 MARCH 2026 
A meeting was held between the Chief Executive, the Management Team of Galway County 
Council, and Oireachtas Members on 30 March 2026 to discuss key strategic, infrastructural 
and funding priorities for County Galway. The meeting provided an opportunity to outline 
the significant challenges facing the Council, particularly in relation to structural 
underfunding when compared with national benchmarks, and to seek support in addressing 
these issues through enhanced central funding mechanisms. It was emphasised that a multi-
year funding correction, including an increase in the Equalisation Fund, is required to ensure 
the sustainable delivery of services.  
A number of major capital and strategic projects were presented, including: 
• 
The Galway City Ring Road, highlighted as a critical strategic infrastructure project 
requiring prioritisation, funding commitment, and advancement through statutory 
processes; 
• 
The proposed redevelopment and transfer of Dunguaire Castle into public 
ownership, with an identified funding requirement of €5 million and ongoing 
engagement with key national agencies; 
• 
The East Galway Wastewater Treatment Plant, identified as essential infrastructure 
to support population growth, housing delivery, and economic development; 
• 
Progress on water services transition and the Craughwell–Clarinbridge wastewater 
scheme, including associated resource and funding implications.  
Updates were also provided on wider economic and spatial development initiatives, 
including the preparation of a joint Economic Development Strategy for Galway City and 
County, ongoing Urban Regeneration and Development Fund (URDF) projects in key towns, 
and the advancement of rail and public realm infrastructure at Oranmore.  
Housing delivery was a key focus of the discussion, with reference to recent measures to 
increase land availability, the use of the Land Acquisition Fund, and significant funding 
applications under the Housing Infrastructure Activation Fund. The Council outlined 
proposals with the potential to deliver substantial additional housing units, subject to 
infrastructure funding and approvals.  
The meeting also included updates on transport and greenway projects, as well as ongoing 
national road schemes, all of which are central to regional connectivity and economic 
development.  
The engagement provided an important platform to communicate the Council’s strategic 
priorities and to advocate for the necessary policy and funding supports from national 
government to enable sustainable growth and service delivery across the County.

LOCAL COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT COMMITTEE 
 
 
The Minister of State with responsibility for Community Development and Charities, Jerry 
Buttimer TD, launched a national awareness campaign on 1 May 2026 to highlight the role 
of Local Community Development Committees (LCDCs) in connecting communities with 
public bodies at local level. The Chief Officer of County Galway LCDC, Lorna Baek, attended 
the official launch event in Cork City. 
As part of the campaign, three LCDCs nationally were selected to participate in the 
development of marketing videos, representing urban, rural and Gaeltacht contexts. Galway 
County LCDC was selected to represent the rural perspective. 
The Galway County suite of videos focus on the Healthy County Galway Dementia Café 
initiative in Connemara as an illustrative example of how LCDCs can support collaborative, 
community-based responses to local needs through partnership working and programme 
alignment. 
The national campaign aims to increase awareness of LCDCs as a key local government 
structure responsible for coordinating community development initiatives and overseeing 
the delivery of programmes such as SICAP, the Local Enhancement Programme and other 
actions aligned with Local Economic and Community Plans (LECPs).

Community groups and volunteers from across County Galway were honoured at the 
Cathaoirleach’s Awards in the Raheen Woods Hotel on Friday night (8th May). 
The event, organised by Galway County Council in partnership with the Galway County 
Public Participation Network, recognised the work of individuals and organisations making a 
difference in their communities. 
 
Hosted by Cathaoirleach Councillor David Collins, the ceremony brought together nominees, 
their families and supporters. MC Ronan Lardner of Galway Bay FM entertained a full house, 
while others tuned in via a live stream on the Council’s Facebook page. 
Among the winners on the night were Make A Difference Youth Club, John Tarpey, the 
Ballinderreen Heritage Publication, Belmont National School, Pop Up Gaeltacht Chinn 
Mhara, Brian Healy, Eyrecourt and District Community Development, St Colman’s Camogie 
Club, Oranmore Tidy Towns, Portumna Tidy Towns, Tuam Women’s Shed and the Fionn 
Science Project. 
Each recipient received a specially commissioned award designed and crafted by Craughwell 
artist Seán Mahony, along with a certificate and a €500 prize to support their work. 
 
Two additional honours were presented on the night. The Cathaoirleach’s Special 
Recognition Award was awarded posthumously to Damien Delaney of Lackagh, 
Turloughmore. He was remembered for his commitment to his community, his involvement 
in local activities and his support for heritage initiatives. The Lifetime Achievement Award  
was presented to Jarlath McDonagh from Turloughmore. A former teacher and public 
representative, he has made a significant contribution to community life, education and 
sport over several decades, including his work with Galway County Council and Seanad 
Éireann.

KILLERERIN - BARNADERG 
Killererin Community Centre in Barnaderg is a vital hub within the local community, 
providing space for social, recreational, educational and youth activities. Prior to works 
commencing, the roof structure had significantly deteriorated, with ageing slates, weather 
damage and defective timber elements posing a risk to the long-term usability and safety of 
the building.  In 2024, as part of a phased redevelopment plan, the centre was closed to 
facilitate essential refurbishment works, with roof replacement identified as a critical 
priority to protect the building fabric and enable future internal upgrades.  The original 
building dates to 1895.  The project was led by Killererin Community Council CLG, who have 
operated the facility which was held by St. Jarlath’s Diocesan Trust. The project cost over 
48k with CLÁR providing 90% funding and 10% provide by the local community via the 
Community Council. Works were completed in May 2026.   
The Centre has secured further funding under the Community Centre Investment Fund CCIF 
and is finalised internal electrical upgrades. With the new roof and upgrades electrics the 
project paves the way for considering Green Energy solutions such as PV panels to further 
future-proof the facility.

It has been another busy and fascinating period, with a wide range of enquiries highlighting 
the depth and diversity of interest in the collections. 
EMAIL ENQUIRIES 
We received approximately 45 email enquiries, covering an impressive variety of topics. 
Many related to family history research, with people tracing ancestors and seeking specific 
details from the records. One such enquiry involved locating the date of birth of a child born 
on Árainn in the early 1900s, successfully uncovered through a combined search of the 
1901 Census and irishgenealogy.ie.

ancestor who had been an inmate of Mountbellew Workhouse before being sent to 
Australia under an assisted emigration scheme in 1851, travelling aboard the ship Palestine. 
Remarkably, detailed information about this woman was found in the digitised Board of 
Guardian Minutes and workhouse records held in the Council Archives.

to connect researchers with valuable archival sources.

information on Encumbered Estates Court rental books, access to photographs of Galway

The concept of end-of-waste established in the European Waste Framework Directive (WFD) 
was adopted in domestic law through Article 28 of the European Communities (Waste 
Directive) Regulations 2011, as amended.   End-of-waste status gives waste holders the 
opportunity to demonstrate, with an appropriate level of rigour, that: 
A waste material can be ‘fully recovered’ and no longer be defined as waste. 
The waste can be used as a ‘secondary’ resource in place of and fulfilling the same role as a 
non-waste derived or virgin ‘primary’ resource. 
New innovations can transform waste into a valuable resource. 
The fully recovered material can be used without causing overall adverse impacts to the 
environment or human health.

presenting a single chronological narrative, the book captures the human stories behind the 
uniform, highlighting the experiences of retired members alongside contributions from 
historians and local voices. These pieces provide valuable context and community 
perspectives, enriching the historical narrative with local voices and insights. 
Chief Superintendent of the Galway Garda Division, Gerry Roche, said he hoped readers 
would find the book engaging and informative. “It is a reflection not only of local policing 
history, but of the social and cultural fabric of Galway through the lens of the Garda 
service,” he said.
